delta_name: Wire RC dominance vs cell delay
at_28nm: At 28nm, path delay ~60% cell, ~40% net. Wire resistance ~0.1 ohm/um on M3-M4, capacitance dominates. Timing fix by sizing cell or swapping VT often enough.
at_7nm_5nm: At 7nm/5nm, M0-M2 resistance ~0.8-1.5 ohm/um, 8-10x higher than 28nm M3. Lower layers wire RC is 70-80% of path for nets >30um. Cell sizing alone does not close timing; need layer promotion and detour reduction.
why_it_changed: Wire cross-section scales ~0.7x per node but resistivity rises due to surface scattering and barrier thickness not scaling. Capacitance per um stays similar, so RC per um scales inverse. Via resistance also 5-8x higher.
what_breaks: 28nm-trained engineer tries to fix -80ps setup by upsizing driver from X2 to X4. At 7nm on M2, net delay drops 5ps but cell delay improves 15ps, still fails, while added capacitance worsens IR and congestion. Symptom: timing wall that does not move with sizing, TNS stuck.
workflow_impact: Placement must be timing-aware to keep critical nets <20um on low layers; routing layer assignment and useful skew become primary fixes, not cell sizing. Added stage: early wire-estimation with real RC and layer-aware placement.

at_28nm: Congestion at 28nm is global-route overflow in macro channels and high-utilization regions. Overflow 2-3% indicates unroutable. Fix by expanding channels, adding halo, lowering utilization.
at_7nm_5nm: At 7nm, global route overflow can be 0% but detailed route still has 5000 DRCs clustered at cell pins and via arrays. Congestion is local pin-access, not channel. M1-M2 tracks blocked by PG and cell architecture.
why_it_changed: Standard-cell height shrank to 6-7 tracks, M1-M2 used for internal cell routing, leaving 2-3 tracks for signal access. Via enclosure rules and single-pattern M0-M1 require larger keepouts, so pin access window shrinks.
what_breaks: 28nm engineer sees 0% overflow and thinks routable, runs detailed route and gets 4000 shorts at macro pins and std-cell pins. Tries more iterations, but DRCs stay at same locations. Symptom: DRC count flat after 3 iterations, all at cell pins, not spread.
workflow_impact: New step: pin-access checker before detailed route, and placement-stage DRC screening. Library selection now driven by pin-access score, not just leakage.

at_28nm: At 28nm, DRCs are mostly spacing/short, fixed by router with 2-3 iterations. Via enclosure is generous, double via insertion is safe.
at_7nm_5nm: At 7nm, 30-50% of DRCs are via enclosure, min area, and via spacing, especially when router inserts via arrays for EM. Via1 and V0 enclosure to M1 requires precise alignment to manufacturing grid, off-grid causes unfixable violations.
why_it_changed: M1 pitch ~36-42nm, via size ~18nm, enclosure ~5nm. Overlay tolerance and EUV edge placement error mean enclosure rules tightened. Single via has high resistance, so double via required for EM, but double via needs more area that conflicts with min area.
what_breaks: 28nm engineer enables automatic double via everywhere to help EM, then gets 2000 via enclosure DRCs that router cannot fix without ripping up M1. Tries to waive as 'via will be fixed later', but they are real manufacturing violations causing yield loss.
workflow_impact: Via rule handling moved into placement and routing as first-class: selective double via only on non-critical layers, via farm control, and early manufacturing grid snap check.

at_28nm: At 28nm, PG mesh on M4-M7, pitch ~30-50um, occupies ~15-20% of routing tracks. IR drop <50mV with moderate density. Routing resource abundant.
at_7nm_5nm: At 7nm, PG needs M0-M1 stripes inside cells plus M3-M5 mesh with pitch 2-5um to meet IR <5% VDD (0.75V). PG occupies 35-45% of M2-M4 tracks. IR drop becomes timing limiter.
why_it_changed: VDD scaled 0.9V to 0.75V to 0.65V, so allowable IR drop budget shrinks from 90mV to 35mV. Current density rises due to higher cell density (2x) and lower VDD, requiring lower resistance PG. Metal resistivity rise makes lower-layer PG less effective, so need more straps.
what_breaks: 28nm engineer uses same PG pitch at 7nm to save routing tracks, gets dynamic IR 80-120mV hotspot that degrades timing 80ps and causes EM violations on M1 PG. Fixes by spreading cells, which worsens congestion because tracks already scarce.
workflow_impact: Floorplan now does PG and placement co-optimization; IR analysis runs after placement, not after route. Need decap insertion 10-15% area and bump planning early.

at_28nm: At 28nm, single patterning for all layers. No coloring. Placement can place any cell anywhere on row without color check.
at_7nm_5nm: At 7nm, M0-M3 are EUV or SAQP with self-aligned double patterning for some layers. Requires two-color or three-color decomposition; odd-cycle violations occur if cell pins with same color are too close. Placement must be color-compliant.
why_it_changed: Pitch below 40nm exceeds single exposure lithography resolution for 193i; EUV still needs double patterning for some layers, and SADP requires alternating mandrel/trim. Physical design must guarantee decomposable layout.
what_breaks: 28nm engineer places cells abutting that create M1 color conflict odd-cycle. DRC reports coloring violation not fixable by router, requires cell spreading or flipping. Symptom: DRCs that appear only after coloring check, not in normal spacing check, clustered at cell abutment.
workflow_impact: New check: color-compliant placement and post-placement coloring verification. Library provides pre-colored cells. Placement tool must honor color spacing rules.

at_28nm: At 28nm, 2-3 VTs (HVT, SVT, LVT) plus maybe ULVT. Vt swapping is primary leakage vs speed tradeoff. Simple: LVT for critical, HVT for non-critical.
at_7nm_5nm: At 7nm/5nm, 5-7 VTs plus multiple channel lengths (e.g., 4-5 lengths) giving continuous tradeoff. Libraries have 100+ variants per function. Continuous Vt mixing with gate-length bias for leakage and variation.
why_it_changed: FinFET and GAA have better subthreshold but variation and leakage still high; to meet power, need fine-grained Vt to avoid overuse of LVT which has 5-10x leakage vs HVT. Channel length bias gives additional 15-20% leakage reduction with small speed cost.
what_breaks: 28nm engineer uses only LVT for all timing fixes, gets leakage 3x budget and IR drop death at 7nm. Or uses HVT everywhere to save power, gets setup wall that cannot close. Symptom: power vs timing Pareto never converges.
workflow_impact: Synthesis and placement use multi-Vt optimization with leakage power as cost, not just timing. Need power-aware placement and Vt-aware IR analysis.

delta_name: Hold closure from afterthought to main effort
at_28nm: At 28nm, hold violations few hundred ps after CTS, fixed with small delay cells, usually 1-2 iterations. Clock skew moderate, OCV small.
at_7nm_5nm: At 7nm, hold wall is thousands of paths, -50 to -150ps, after CTS with low VDD and high variation. Hold fixing competes with setup and congestion, requires large delay cells that hurt area and power.
why_it_changed: Lower VDD reduces cell delay, but clock insertion grows due to high wire RC, making short data vs long clock path worse. Variation (AOCV/POCV) for hold is larger relative to path delay (30% of path vs 10% at 28nm).
what_breaks: 28nm engineer fixes setup first, then adds hold buffers at end, creating congestion that breaks setup again, loop never ends. Or uses zero hold uncertainty at 7nm, gets silicon hold failure that cannot be fixed by frequency reduction.
workflow_impact: Hold-aware CTS and useful skew from start, hold uncertainty 30-60ps budgeted early, and simultaneous setup/hold optimization instead of sequential.

delta_name: Utilization target drop and whitespace reservation
at_28nm: At 28nm, target utilization 75-80% achievable with 5-10% whitespace for ECO. Design closes with 70-75% final density.
at_7nm_5nm: At 7nm/5nm, target utilization 60-68% for routability, with 10-15% explicit decap and spare cell area. Final density 60% is considered high.
why_it_changed: Pin access, PG overhead, and via rules consume tracks that utilization metric does not count. At 7nm, effective routing capacity per cell is ~60% of 28nm due to track loss to PG and coloring keepouts.
what_breaks: 28nm engineer sets 75% utilization at 7nm to meet area, gets 0% overflow but 8000 DRCs at pin access and IR drop >100mV, plus no space for hold buffers. Must expand floorplan 10-15% late.
workflow_impact: Floorplan reserves decap and spare cell area up front, and utilization target set by routability and IR, not area. Early congestion and IR checks gate placement.

at_28nm: At 28nm, signoff with 4-6 corners: SS/TT/FF, hot/cold, with flat OCV derate 5-10% for setup/hold. AOCV table optional.
at_7nm_5nm: At 7nm/5nm, 20-30 corners: SS/TT/FF with low/high VDD (0.65-0.85V), hot/cold, plus 5-7 RC corners, plus AOCV/POCV with distance and voltage derate. CRPR and IR-aware corners added.
why_it_changed: Low VDD makes delay highly voltage sensitive, and FinFET variation due to fin height, work-function, and EUV LER increases. Wire RC variation dominates due to thin barriers, requiring separate RC corners. Voltage droop is corner-dependent.
what_breaks: 28nm engineer signs off at TT only with flat derate, misses slow-low-voltage corner that is 25% slower than SS at nominal VDD, causing speed bin failure. Or misses RC max corner causing setup failure on long nets only.
workflow_impact: STA runs expanded to multi-corner multi-mode with POCV; need efficient corner pruning and machine learning for corner reduction. Timing ECO must fix across all corners, not just worst.
